title: Contention-Aware Forecasting of Energy Efficiency through Sequence-Based Models in Modern Heterogeneous Processors
problem: Energy efficiency in heterogeneous processors is highly variable across core types, voltage/frequency levels, and application phases with resource contention, making static optimization ineffective. Accurate prediction of efficiency under dynamic contention scenarios is missing.
motivation: Energy-constrained embedded and edge systems demand proactive resource management to optimize power consumption under varying workloads and contention in clustered heterogeneous processors.
method: EffiCast leverages LSTM and Transformer sequence models trained on structured data capturing energy efficiency sensitivities across heterogeneous cores, V/f levels, application phases, and contention patterns. The models forecast future system states to enable dynamic resource management with inference latency of 1.82 ms per sequence on real processors.
key_novelty: First contention-aware energy efficiency forecasting methodology for heterogeneous processors using sequence-based deep learning models instead of static predictors.
contributions: Comprehensive sensitivity analysis of energy efficiency across core types, V/f levels, application phases, and resource contention in heterogeneous processors
Novel LSTM and Transformer-based sequence models achieving unprecedented forecast accuracy
Deployment on real heterogeneous processors with Intel oneDNN acceleration achieving 1.82 ms inference latency
Demonstrated integration into proactive resource management frameworks for dynamic optimization

metrics.accuracy: SOTA prediction accuracy vs. state-of-the-art techniques

baselines: state-of-the-art predictive techniques for energy efficiency
primary_theme: Contention-aware energy efficiency prediction in heterogeneous processors
